title: Breakthrough: one tempo flips the result
outcomes: Counts the pawn moves after the sacrifice to check who queens first
Predicts that giving the other side the move can turn a win into a loss for the first side
Checks his count against a verified result and finds which step was miscounted

steps.text: In *Breakthrough: who wins when the pawns meet* you predicted results. Now check by counting. After the pawn sacrifice, count the moves each side's remaining passed pawn needs to queen; the side to move takes the first of them. Do this in your head before you answer.

steps.caption: The count for the first position. White to move; Black could also take on f4, and the tablebase says White wins either way.

line.say: White pushes g5. Now either black pawn can take a white pawn: this is the sacrifice.
Black takes on e4. That pawn needs three moves to queen: e3, e2, e1.
White's g-pawn also needs three moves (g6, g7, g8) and has already started: one move ahead.
Black's king is far from the g-file and cannot stop the pawn.
One step from the last rank.
Black's pawn is still one move behind.
White queens first and, by the tablebase, still wins from here.

claims.statement: After g5 White wins with best play (tablebase, exact).
The position is a win for White to move (tablebase, exact).

steps.title: The same skeleton, the other side to move
steps.prompt: In the first position White, to move, wins. Now Black is to move and nothing else changes. Predict the result for Black, then look at the third position, where only a king moved.

steps.text: **One tempo (one move) can reverse the result.** In these skeletons the side to move wins; give the other side the move and it wins instead. This is true for these positions (tablebase), not a law for all skeletons: kings near the pawns, or pawns further back, can change it. Count first, then check against the position.

steps.prompt: Look at the answer you got wrong or were unsure of. Which count was off: your pawn, the other pawn, or who moves first?

sources: Items IE-BRK-4 to 12 and IBds72-3: tablebase results (7 pieces); the claim about the side to move holds for these skeletons only
